claims.text: The initial as-cast CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase FCC solid solution.
Long-term high-cycle fatigue loading at 300–400 °C causes the FCC CoCrFeMnNi alloy to develop nanoscale phase separation.
The proposed nanoscale phase separation occurs through spinodal decomposition or precipitation.
Phase separation reduces local ductility in CoCrFeMnNi.
Reduced local ductility caused by phase separation promotes brittle fracture.
Spinodal decomposition or nanoscale precipitation begins in grain interiors and at grain boundaries.
The combination of cyclic stress and moderate-temperature exposure induces chemical inhomogeneities in CoCrFeMnNi.
The induced chemical inhomogeneities produce nanoscale phase separation.
The proposed microstructural change facilitates crack initiation.
Crack initiation associated with phase separation leads to reduced toughness and eventual brittle fracture.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, cyclically loaded specimens will exhibit a gradual deterioration in toughness.
Nanometer-scale phase separation will be detectable by high-resolution TEM or atom probe tomography in regions prone to brittle fracture.
The proposed behavior applies to power-generation service involving cyclic loading at temperatures up to 400 °C.
High mixing entropy may limit the kinetic feasibility or extent of spinodal decomposition in CoCrFeMnNi.
